subject: Public Comment Submission
comment: Input In Advance of Council's Dec. 14 Vote: DV Right of Way Vacation Petition Dear Council, We are the owners of 1955 Deer Valley Dr. N, Unit 405, and we do not support Deer Valley's right of way petition for the 2.6 acres of public roadway that Alterra wants the City to vacate in order to allow Deer Valley to build a ski beach over the road. Our questions and concerns in this matter: 1. There is no transparency concerning the details of the 'partnership' between the City and Deer Valley. 2. We do not see a net tangible community benefit as mandated for both our immediate neighborhood and the City as a whole. 3. There needs to be an updated traffic study that substantiates that daily traffic to Snow Park will be mitigated by a15-20% reduction in parking at Snow Park and a Mayflower portal. 4. We are strongly opposed to the altered circulation pattern and 34% increase in daily traffic that would result from the right of way vacation and its associated development. Residents, pedestrians, cyclists and properties would absolutely be affected by more vehicles using fewer roadways. The ensuing noise and air pollution increases are unacceptable. 5. State and and municipal code governing right of way vacations are clear and specify that there must be good cause to vacate, there can be no harm to any property owner, the right of way must not have any utility, and there must be a net tangible benefit to award the right of way. We maintain that Deer Valley’s current proposal and the announced “deal” do not meet necessary standards as outlined. ~Deanna Sharp 1955 Deer Valley Dr. N., #405 Park City, UT 84060

subject: Council Letter - Snow Park Development
comment: Dear Mayor, Councilor and Park City Team, I know that you are receiving significant feedback from constituents regarding the proposed agreement with Deer Valley, and I thought it may be helpful to lend my voice to the discussion. I've come to know you each over the last year, and I appreciate the diligence and gratitude you all put into your work. It's with that spirit that I and others have watched you negotiate a strong deal with Deer Valley; one that will benefit the community for decades to come. I am not sure if some Park City residents recognize that this is not a binary decision - that DV has come to the table to work with you in a spirit of partnership and not because they have no other option. In my opinion, such partnerships between elected officials and our largest local private enterprises is essential to manage growth, protect the spirit of Park City and ensure that only the best ideas are pursued. The alternative to this type of partnership is long, protracted battles between residents, government and companies with no clear winners. As the representatives for your communities, you've done admirable work. You've studied the nuances and idiosyncrasies of the options, listened to considerable public input and negotiated in good faith. Your proposed solution is elegant and progressive and one that deserves support from all of us. Thank you for everything you've done to secure real, important gains for our community. From the affordable housing to the regional transportation hub to the reduction in parking spaces, the plan's benefits will live on for years. Sincerely, -Scott van Hartesvelt (He/Him) Founder c. (435) 640-6967 w. www.gcommercesolutions.com

subject: Public Comment Submission
comment: Tuesday, December 5, 2023 Dear Mayor Worel and City Council Members: I am requesting that City Council VOTE NO on the Deer Valley Road Vacation for Alterra/Deer Valley’s Snow Park Development. As a full time resident of Park City, I am lending my voice to the public process. I am hopeful that City Council will consider the will of the people and advocate on behalf of Park City residents with Alterra/Deer Valley to come to a more agreeable partnership with greater immediate and long term financial impacts. The City Council should not outright transfer rights of Deer Valley Loop to Alterra as outlined in the partnership agreement that Mayor Worel announced. Why? Alterra/Deer Valley’s Snow Park Development poses serious challenges to the residents of Deer Valley and adjacent neighborhoods. We will be negatively affected by the increase in traffic during the construction of and upon completion of this project. Air pollution and significant noise pollution from increased traffic pose serious health risks for every person that lives, works, and recreates in this region. No mention of these impacts have ever been addressed by either City Council or Alterra/Deer Valley in a public forum. To mitigate this material harm to people and the environment, Alterra/Deer Valley has the responsibility to be a good neighbor and provide ongoing financial resources to offset the irreparable and negative environmental impacts on this community. The stated amount of $15 million seems arbitrary and $15 million is just not enough! In addition, Alterra/Deer Valley should be good partners and conduct a new traffic study to fully assess the environmental impacts of their project. On a personal note, the increase in traffic from this project directly affects my ability to respond to emergency surgeries at Park City Hospital, as needed. As a healthcare provider, I am frequently on call for emergency surgeries that require me to be at the hospital within 30 minutes. Depending upon the time of day, my commute, which is usually 10 minutes, during peak traffic times can be 60 minutes or more. While I have a unique perspective on this traffic issue, I am not the only person impacted. I am against the road vacation, and I ask City Council members to VOTE NO. Respectfully, Kristin Gentile, DNP, APRN 555 Deer Valley Drive Park City, UT 84060 (206) 550-8920

subject: Public Comment Submission
comment: Dear Madam Mayor, Dear Council Members, First and foremost, thank you for the hard work you and your teams are doing on behalf of all the Park City citizens - balancing the variety of opinions in any community in a sensible way is a challenging feat on the eve of 2024. For all our leaders on Council, incoming, outgoing and/or already serving, I wish you well, and I hope you all continue to hear and listen prior to deciding. As it relates to the topic at stake in the header of this email, I have mixed feelings about the outcomes and potentially missed opportunities. I certainly hope Council and Deer Valley can answer many questions in the spirit of transparency of a PPP. While Deer Valley pays $15M towards the creation of a regionally significant transportation and parking facility, how does it compare vs. the savings realized to decrease parking capacity by 1520%? While Deer Valley boasts a "new portal and base area via U.S. Route 40, bypassing Park City", this was planned as a part of the Expanded Excellence. Deer Valley will undoubtedly raise its Comfortable Carrying Capacity (CCC). I have yet to see data that inform the public whether the increase in capacity at this new entry point/portal is more than the planned incremental CCC. If not, we have not altered the capacity much destined to Snow Park, and as such traffic issues will persist. I would rather the PPP contain a plan to open an incremental entry point that currently does not exist or the alteration of an existing under-utilized entry point. I commend Deer Valley and Park City for their continued push into affordable housing. I do hope that the units just announced are not encompassed in the previously announced project on Iron Horse Dr and are incremental to it. Other ideas and concepts presented in the PPP summary are worthy of attention and undoubtedly commendable in many ways. All in all, I feel the PCMC seized the moment, but the need for a more daring outcome as part of a PPP was not achieved. Other tools and mechanisms are at your disposal to turn this development into a more significant achievement for Park City, and I hope they are considered. Respectfully, Hervé Lavenant
